findings.message: writes to system directories or boot locations
findings.remediation: Restrict file writes to user-owned directories with explicit approval.
findings.impact: System startup and installation directories are sensitive destinations for persistent modification.
findings.attack_vector: Source references a boot or system directory; this low lead does not by itself prove mutation or privilege.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.impact: Extremely long lines hide obfuscated or minified code from human review.

findings.message: downloads and pipes code directly to interpreter (3 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Do not execute code downloaded at runtime; pin and review shipped code.
findings.impact: Downloading and piping remote code to an interpreter gives attackers full RCE on the CI runner.
findings.attack_vector: curl/wget output piped to bash/node/python — no checksum verification on fetched content.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: detects net.connect, dgram.createSocket, or process-level network access
findings.remediation: Review all network connections; ensure they use allowlisted destinations with explicit approval.
findings.impact: Raw TCP/UDP sockets bypass HTTP-level monitoring and allow covert data channels.
findings.attack_vector: net.connect() or dgram.createSocket() — traffic is invisible to HTTP-based DLP.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
